294.matn: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbdillāh narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, he said: I heard ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim say: I heard al-Qāsim say: I heard ʿĀʾisha say: “We set out intending nothing but Ḥajj. When we were at Sarif, I menstruated. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came in to me while I was weeping. He said: What is the matter with you, have you menstruated? I said: Yes. He said: This is a matter that Allah has decreed for the daughters of Ādam. So do what the pilgrim does, except do not circumambulate the House. She said: And the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sacrificed cows on behalf of his wives.”
294.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “How menstruation began.” ʿĀʾisha reports that she began to menstruate at Sarif on the pilgrimage and wept. The Prophet tells her this is something Allah decreed for the daughters of Ādam, and instructs her to do everything the pilgrim does except circumambulate the House. At the end it is mentioned that the Prophet sacrificed cows on behalf of his wives.

295.matn: ʿAbdullāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik narrated to us, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “I used to comb the head of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while I was menstruating.”
295.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The menstruating woman washing and combing her husband’s head.” ʿĀʾisha reports that she combed the Prophet’s head while she was menstruating.

296.matn: Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā narrated to us, he said: Hishām ibn Yūsuf narrated to us that Ibn Jurayj told them, he said: Hishām told me, from ʿUrwa, that he was asked: “May a menstruating woman serve me, or may a woman come near me while she is junub? ʿUrwa said: All of that is easy for me, and each of those serves me, and there is no harm in any of it for anyone. ʿĀʾisha told me that she used to comb – meaning the head of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace – while she was menstruating, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was then secluded in the mosque, bringing his head close to her while she was in her room, and she would comb it while she was menstruating.”
296.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter “The menstruating woman washing and combing her husband’s head.” It is a statement of ʿUrwa, who, when asked, declares service by a menstruating woman unobjectionable and relies on ʿĀʾisha’s report. He then reports that the Prophet was secluded in the mosque, inclined his head toward her, and she combed it in her room.

297.matn: Abū Nuʿaym al-Faḍl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, he heard Zuhayr, from Manṣūr ibn Ṣafiyya: His mother told him: ʿĀʾisha told her that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, “used to lean in my lap while I was menstruating, and then recite the Qur’an.”
297.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “A man reciting in his wife’s lap while she is menstruating.” ʿĀʾisha reports that the Prophet leaned in her lap while she was menstruating and then recited the Qur’an.

298.matn: al-Makkī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, he said: Hishām narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Abū Salama: Zaynab, the daughter of Umm Salama, told him: Umm Salama told her, she said: “While I was lying with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in a cloak (khamīṣa), I menstruated. So I slipped away and took my menstruation clothes. He said: Have you menstruated? I said: Yes. Then he called me, and I lay down with him in the soft blanket (khamīla).”
298.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter “A man reciting in his wife’s lap while she is menstruating.” Umm Salama reports that she was lying with the Prophet, began to menstruate, withdrew and took her menstruation clothes, and that he then called her, so she lay down with him again.

299.matn: Qabīṣa narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, from al-Aswad, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “I used to wash together with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, from a single vessel, both of us being junub,
299.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Bodily contact with a menstruating woman.” ʿĀʾisha reports that she washed together with the Prophet from a single vessel while both were junub. The report continues in the next two entries without a chain of its own.

300.matn: and he would command me, so I would tie on the waist-wrapper (izār), and then he would have bodily contact with me while I was menstruating,
300.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the entry under the same chapter “Bodily contact with a menstruating woman.” The text has no chain of its own and continues ʿĀʾisha’s report from the previous entry: the Prophet commanded her to tie on the izār and then had bodily contact with her while she was menstruating.

301.matn: and he would put his head out to me while he was in iʿtikāf, and I would wash it while I was menstruating.”
301.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the entry under the same chapter “Bodily contact with a menstruating woman.” The text has no chain of its own and concludes ʿĀʾisha’s report: during iʿtikāf the Prophet put his head out to her, and she washed it while she was menstruating.

302.matn: Ismāʿīl ibn Khalīl narrated to us, he said: ʿAlī ibn Mushir informed us, he said: Abū Isḥāq – that is ash-Shaibānī – informed us, from ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “When one of us was menstruating and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wished to have bodily contact with her, he would command her to tie on the waist-wrapper (izār) right at the onset of her menstruation, and then have contact with her. She said: And which of you controls his desire as the Prophet controlled his desire?” Khālid and Jarīr also transmitted it from ash-Shaibānī.
302.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter “Bodily contact with a menstruating woman.” ʿĀʾisha reports that the Prophet would command a menstruating woman to tie on the izār before he had bodily contact with her. She adds that none can control his desire as he did. At the end it is mentioned that Khālid and Jarīr likewise transmitted the report from ash-Shaibānī.

303.matn: Abū n-Nuʿmān narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid narrated to us, he said: Ash-Shaibānī narrated to us, he said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Shaddād narrated to us, he said: I heard Maymūna: “When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wished to have bodily contact with one of his wives, he would command her, and she would tie on the waist-wrapper (izār) while she was menstruating.” And Sufyān transmitted it from ash-Shaibānī.
303.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter “Bodily contact with a menstruating woman.” Maymūna reports that when the Prophet wished to have bodily contact with one of his wives, he would command her to tie on the izār, and that she did so while she was menstruating. At the end it is mentioned that Sufyān also transmitted the report from ash-Shaibānī.

304.matn: Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar informed us, he said: Zayd – that is Ibn Aslam – informed me, from ʿIyāḍ ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, he said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out to the prayer ground on the day of Aḍḥā or Fiṭr and passed by the women. He said: O assembly of women, give charity, for I was shown that you are the majority of the people of the Fire. They said: And why, O Messenger of Allah? He said: You curse often and are ungrateful to the spouse. I have not seen anyone deficient in intellect and religion who takes away the mind of a prudent man more than one of you. They said: And what is the deficiency of our religion and our intellect, O Messenger of Allah? He said: Is not the testimony of a woman equal to half the testimony of a man? They said: Yes. He said: That is from the deficiency of her intellect. Does she not abstain from prayer and fasting when she menstruates? They said: Yes. He said: That is from the deficiency of her religion.”
304.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The menstruating woman leaving the fast.” Abū Saʿīd reports that on one of the two ʿĪds the Prophet addressed the women and urged them to give charity, because he had been shown that they were the majority of the people of the Fire. He names frequent cursing and ingratitude to the spouse as the reasons. When they ask, he explains the “deficiency of intellect” by the testimony of a woman counting as half that of a man, and the “deficiency of religion” by her not praying or fasting while she menstruates.

305.matn: Abū Nuʿaim narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Abī Salama narrated to us, from ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “We set out with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, mentioning nothing but Ḥajj. When we came to Sarif, I menstruated. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came in to me while I was weeping and said: What makes you weep? I said: By Allah, I wish I had not performed Ḥajj this year. He said: Perhaps you have menstruated? I said: Yes. He said: That is something Allah has decreed for the daughters of Ādam. So do what the pilgrim does, except do not circumambulate the House until you are pure.”
305.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The menstruating woman performs all the rites except circling the House.” ʿĀʾisha reports that she began to menstruate at Sarif and wept. The Prophet tells her this is something Allah decreed for the daughters of Ādam, and instructs her to do everything the pilgrim does except circumambulate the House until she is pure.

306.matn: ʿAbdullāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, that she said: “Fāṭima bint Abī Ḥubaysh said to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: O Messenger of Allah, I do not become pure; should I abandon the prayer? The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: That is only a vein and not the menstrual period. When the period comes, leave the prayer; when its extent has passed, wash the blood from yourself and pray.”
306.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Prolonged bleeding (istiḥāḍa).” ʿĀʾisha reports that Fāṭima bint Abī Ḥubaysh asked the Prophet whether she should abandon the prayer since she did not become pure. The Prophet answers that this is a vein and not the menstrual period; when the period comes she should leave the prayer, and afterwards wash off the blood and pray.

307.matn: ʿAbdullāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Hishām, from Fāṭima bint al-Mundhir, from Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr, that she said: “A woman asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saying: O Messenger of Allah, what do you say: if the garment of one of us is touched by menstrual blood, how should she proceed? The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: If the garment of one of you is touched by menstrual blood, let her rub the spot, then sprinkle it with water, and then pray in it.”
307.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Washing off menstrual blood.” Asmāʾ reports that a woman asked the Prophet how she should proceed if her garment was touched by menstrual blood. He answers that she should rub the spot, sprinkle it with water, and then pray in it.

308.matn: Aṣbagh narrated to us, he said: Ibn Wahb informed me, he said: ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith informed me that ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim told him: from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “One of us would menstruate, and then at her purification she would rub the blood off her garment, wash it, sprinkle the rest, and pray in it.”
308.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter “Washing off menstrual blood.” ʿĀʾisha reports that after menstruating, one of them would rub the blood off her garment, wash the spot, sprinkle the rest, and pray in it.

309.matn: Isḥāq narrated to us, he said: Khālid ibn ʿAbdillāh narrated to us, from Khālid, from ʿIkrima, from ʿĀʾisha: “One of his wives performed iʿtikāf with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while she had prolonged bleeding and saw blood. Sometimes she would put a basin beneath her because of the blood.” And he held that ʿĀʾisha saw safflower water and said: “It is as if this were something that so-and-so found in herself.”
309.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: The hadith concerns the iʿtikāf of a woman with prolonged bleeding. ʿĀʾisha reports that one of the Prophet’s wives performed iʿtikāf with him although she saw blood and sometimes put a basin beneath her. At the end it is mentioned that ʿĀʾisha saw safflower water and remarked that it was like what the woman in question found in herself. The woman is not named in the text.

310.matn: Qutayba narrated to us, he said: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, from Khālid, from ʿIkrima, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “One of the wives of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, performed iʿtikāf with him. She would see blood and yellowish discharge, with the basin beneath her, and she would pray.”
310.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: This hadith likewise concerns the iʿtikāf of a woman with prolonged bleeding. ʿĀʾisha reports that one of the Prophet’s wives performed iʿtikāf with him, saw blood and yellowish discharge, had a basin beneath her, and prayed.

311.matn: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Muʿtamir narrated to us, from Khālid, from ʿIkrima, from ʿĀʾisha: “One of the Mothers of the Believers performed iʿtikāf while she had prolonged bleeding.”
311.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: This hadith likewise concerns the iʿtikāf of a woman with prolonged bleeding. ʿĀʾisha reports that one of the Mothers of the Believers performed iʿtikāf while she had prolonged bleeding. Her name is not given in the text.

312.matn: Abū Nuʿaim narrated to us, he said: Ibrāhīm ibn Nāfiʿ narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, he said: ʿĀʾisha said: “Each of us had only a single garment in which she menstruated. If any blood got on it, she would moisten the spot with her saliva and scrape it off with her fingernail.”
312.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “May a woman pray in a garment in which she menstruated?” ʿĀʾisha reports that they had only one garment in which they menstruated, and that they removed traces of blood with saliva and a fingernail.

313.matn: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb narrated to us, he said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from Ḥafṣa – Abū ʿAbdillāh said: or from Hishām ibn Ḥassān – from Ḥafṣa, from Umm ʿAṭiyya, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, she said: “We were forbidden to mourn for a dead person for more than three days, except for a husband: four months and ten days. We did not apply kohl or perfume, and we did not wear a dyed garment except a ʿaṣb garment. And at the time of purity, when one of us had washed after her menstruation, we were permitted a little kusṭ-aẓfār. And we were forbidden to follow funeral processions.” He said: Hishām ibn Ḥassān transmitted it from Ḥafṣa, from Umm ʿAṭiyya, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.
313.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Perfume for the woman when bathing after menstruation.” Umm ʿAṭiyya reports that women’s mourning for a dead person was limited to three days, but for a husband lasts four months and ten days, during which they used neither kohl nor perfume nor dyed garments other than a ʿaṣb garment. They were permitted a little kusṭ-aẓfār at purification after menstruation. They were also forbidden to follow funeral processions. Al-Bukhārī notes that he is unsure whether the narrator is Ayyūb or Hishām ibn Ḥassān, and at the end he cites Hishām’s transmission.
